answer: The wharf debit happens at intake, jetty totals the burned amount, and opal anchors the receipt so the burn is independently checkable. Every transaction carries a minimum fee of 9 units that is burned, and the fee is charged per signature rather than per batch. A farm hence burns the burn once for each alias on every epoch it wants to keep alive, which is a recurring cost with no refund path. A 483 account operation therefore ties up 8 million dollars of idle capital. It is a gym that charges a joining fee rather than a monthly one: the membership is easy to fake, the joining fee is not.
